name: Plainproof: Home Inventory
subtitle: Belongings list for insurance

description:
After a fire, a flood or a break-in, an insurer asks for a list of everything you owned, with proof. Plainproof is where you keep that list before you need it.

Go room by room. For each thing, take a photo, note the brand, model and serial number, what you paid and what it would cost to replace, and snap the receipt if you still have it. It takes about a minute an item.

- A report your insurer can use: every item by room with its photo, serial number, purchase details and value, and a total for each room and for the whole home, as a PDF you can send or print
- Claim mode: after a loss, mark what was stolen, damaged, destroyed or lost, add the claim number and what happened, and get the schedule of loss your insurer asks for. Each loss is its own claim, and several can be open at once
- A claim package: one file for the adjuster with the schedule, a spreadsheet, every photo and receipt in a folder per item, the room videos and your policy
- A spreadsheet of the same details, for an adjuster's own forms
- Walk-through videos of each room, to show what a list can miss
- Your policy kept with your things, and a check of your belongings against its limits
- Read a serial number off its label, and the date, shop and price off a receipt, with the camera
- Warranty dates, and reminders to look the list over, to back up and before a warranty ends
- Rooms you name yourself, with a running total for each
- A list of what still needs a photo, a value or a serial number, so the gaps are easy to close
- Search by name, brand or serial number
- A backup you control: one file with every item, photo, video and document, saved wherever you choose and restored on a new iPhone, or saved by itself to a folder in iCloud Drive if you turn that on
- Dark mode, and text that follows your iPhone's text size

Nothing leaves your iPhone unless you send it. There is no account to create and no server: your inventory is stored in the app, and you decide where a report or a backup goes. The automatic backup is off until you choose a folder for it. Keep a backup somewhere other than the phone, since a list that is lost along with the house is no use.

Free for your first 20 items in one place, with every feature. Plainproof Pro removes the limit and adds more places, such as a rental, an office or a storage unit, with one payment. It is not a subscription, and nothing you have added is ever locked: the report and backups keep working when the free version is full.

Values are your own figures. Plainproof does not appraise anything, and insurers differ in what they accept, so ask yours what a claim needs.

support._about: This app's section on the apps' support page (tools/site_pages.py). Every answer must match what the app shows.
support.restore: Open the Settings tab: Restore purchase is in the first group, under Plainproof Pro. It is also at the bottom of the Pro screen.
support.backup: Open the Report tab and scroll down to Backup. Back up now makes one file with every item, photo, video and document: save it to iCloud Drive or a computer, or email it to yourself. To have it done by itself, open the Settings tab, turn on iCloud Drive backup and choose a folder in iCloud Drive. On the new iPhone, open the Report tab and tap Restore from a backup.

more.q: What does the free version include?
more.a: Every feature, for up to 20 items in one place. Plainproof Pro removes the limit and adds more places (a rental, an office, a storage unit) with one payment. Nothing you have added is ever locked: the report and backups keep working when the free version is full.

more.q: How do I make a claim with it?
more.a: Open the Report tab and tap Make a claim, then Start a claim. Choose what was stolen, damaged, destroyed or lost, add the claim number, the date and what happened, and a note on any item. Make the claim package to get one file for the adjuster: the schedule of loss, a spreadsheet, every photo and receipt of those items, the room videos and your policy. A second loss gets its own claim: tap Start another claim on the Report tab, and each claim keeps its own items, details and package. When a claim is settled, End the claim; your items stay.

more.q: Will my insurer accept the report?
more.a: The report lists every item by room with its photo, serial number, purchase details and value, and a total for each room. Insurers differ in what they ask for, so check with yours. The spreadsheet has the same details in a form an adjuster can sort.
They are your own figures. Enter what it would cost to replace the item; if you leave that empty, the price you paid is used. The app does not appraise anything.

review_notes:
Plainproof is a home inventory for insurance claims. There is no account and no sign-in, and the app makes no network calls of its own: everything a person enters stays on the iPhone.

The one in-app purchase is Plainproof Pro (non-consumable, com.gamequarry.plainproof.pro). To see it: open the Settings tab and tap Plainproof Pro. It also opens by itself when the + button is tapped with 20 items already added, or when Add a place is tapped on the Places screen. Pro removes the 20-item limit and allows more than one place. Restore purchase is on the Pro screen and in Settings.

The camera and photo library are used only when a person adds a photo of an item, a receipt or a policy page, records a walk-through video of a room (open a room and tap Add a walk-through video), or reads a serial number or a receipt with the camera. The microphone is used only while a walk-through video is being recorded, so the person can say what things are as they film. Text in photos is read on the device with Apple's Vision framework. Reminders are local notifications, scheduled on the device only after the person turns them on in Settings. The PDF report, the spreadsheet, the claim package and the backup file are made on the device and handed to the share sheet. The optional automatic backup (Settings, iCloud Drive backup; off by default) saves the backup file into a folder the person picks with the system folder picker; the app has no iCloud entitlement and no server of its own.
